raw_segments.text: Coriolanus, you common cry of curse, whose breath I hate as rico th, rotten fens, whose
loves I prize as the dead carcasses of unburied men that do corrupt my heir, I banish you.
And here remain with your uncertainty.
Let every feeble rumor shake your hearts.
Your enemies, with nodding of their plumes, fan you into despair.
Have the power still to banish your defenders, till at length your ignorance, which finds
not till it feels, making but reservation of yourselves, still your own foes, deliver
you as most abated captives to some nation that won you without blows.
Despising for you the city, thus I turn my back.
